B.explanation: Omits "time" (དུས) of the fruition, rendering it just as "their fruits".
Uses "無我" (anatman), but the Tibetan "བདག་མིན" here means "not mine" (amama).

A.explanation: Translates "གཡོགས་པ" as the covering (clothes), but it refers to the covered body.

B.explanation: Substitutes the root text's "if there is no need" with the commentary's explanation "disgusted by impurity".
Likely a typo for "知已" (having known); "知己" (knowing oneself) misses the Tibetan "ཤེས་བྱས་ནས" (having known [this]).
Likely a typo for "托他" or "施他", changing the meaning from "give/entrust to others" to "drag others".

A.span: 未獲佛陀圓滿樂，如是處境絕無有
A.explanation: Misses "other than" (མིན་པ) and "this [suffering]" (འདི), changing the meaning entirely.

B.span: 非屬佛之圓滿樂，如是處境絕無有
B.explanation: Misses that "such a situation" specifically refers to "this" (འདི) current state of suffering.

C.explanation: Adds "great" (大) to the faults of others, which is not in the source text.
Adds "joyfully" (欣然), which is not in the source text.
Translates "de nyid du gzhan yod" (if in reality it exists as another) incorrectly as "the perceived object is different from the real object."

A.explanation: The Tibetan says "whether it is conventional or ultimate," referring to the status of merit, not the "mind" of the worshipper.
"境遇" normally means "circumstances"; using it here to mean "contact with the object" is highly ambiguous and confusing.
The Tibetan states it was analyzed previously (indicative/past), not that it *should be* analyzed (imperative).
The Tibetan specifically says "without a son there is no father," which is lost when paraphrased as "father and son exist mutually."

B.explanation: The Tibetan "der" (there) refers to the state of having obtained discernment, which is more specific than just "this life".

C.explanation: The Tibetan "mnyen" means gentle or affectionate; it does not mean to "benefit" (饒益).

B.span: 有情願悉得，怙主慈護念！
B.explanation: Misses the specific connection "whatever the protectors intend, may beings receive that," adding "compassionately care" instead.
